# socialus-ops

The operating manual for building SocialUs: who does what, what triggers it, what it produces, and where it is broken. No product code here. `CLAUDE.md` holds the rules; this file is the map.

**As of 2026-10-11** · Source: the live repos, workflows, scores and Issues named in each row · Generated by: `regen-readme`

**Snapshot, 2026-10-11.** A point-in-time picture rebuilt from the live repos, never hand-maintained (section 6). Every claim carries **[V]** verified (read or run on the snapshot date, source named) or **[A]** assumed. **[P]** marks a proposal that does not exist yet.

## 1. The chain

```
request / story
  -> plan-feature (council: design + plan)        stops at a brief the PM approves
  -> run-feature-pipeline (any feature, new or built): assess, do the first phase not done, reassess
       phases: filed, planned, ticketed, built, reviewed, shipped, smoked, reported, PM looked
  -> the CRITERION ROLL-UP (section 4): every acceptance criterion scored, rolled up to the dashboard
  -> the PM looks (phone checklist #519, ticks) -> "PM looked" -> launch report (Fridays)
```

Three layers: build (1), observe (2a: dashboard, criterion roll-up, STATUS, launch report), improve the pipeline (2b: the trial in section 7).

## How our work is structured

One hierarchy, used in every generated doc, report, Issue template, dashboard and this README. **[V]** the IDs below exist today; the dashboard, reports and `planning/uat-journeys.json` use them.

```
Area  >  Feature (F###)  >  Journey (J##)  >  Criterion (F###.n)
                  \______ the agents' layer ______/        \__ the unit that builds, tests and scores
                              Journey = the PM's human check, over a set of criteria
```

| Level | ID | Who it is for | Lives in | Rolls up to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Area** | slug: `moderation`, `explore-map`, `create-posts`, `sign-in-you`, `page-editing`, `sharing-links`, `builders-seed`, `ops` | both | `area:<slug>` label; `build-log/reports/<area>/` | milestone |
| **Feature** | `F###` (stable, never reused) | both | `planning/scenario-F###.md`, report `build-log/reports/<area>/F###-<slug>.md` | area |
| **Journey** | `J##` (stable; file `planning/uat-journeys.json`) | the PM: one real flow, 3 minutes, 3-5 look-fors, one link, one role, no criterion ids | phone checklist (socialus-web #519, shows the next four) | area (of its first feature), milestone |
| **Criterion** | `F###.n` (suffix letters allowed, `F059.2b`) | the agents: one testable statement | the feature's report, one row each | feature |

**Two roll-ups, both ending at area and milestone.** Feature progress is counted by **criteria** (built, checked, reviewed, smoked): that is what builds, tests and scores. The PM's review is counted by **journeys** (looked / total): one tick marks every criterion under the journey "PM looked". Each criterion sits under exactly one journey (`uat_journeys.py --check`); criteria with no screen have none and stay with the agents. The dashboard shows both, by area.

**Standard header.** Within the first 15 lines of every doc that describes state, one line:

`**As of YYYY-MM-DD** · Source: <what it is read from> · Generated by: <skill or script>` for a generated doc, or `... · Maintained by: hand (<owner>)` for a hand-written one.

Exempt, because their format is fixed elsewhere: build-log ticket entries and weekly indexes (history), per-feature criterion reports and `planning/scenario-F###.md` (frontmatter and the report grammar carry the dates), `SKILL.md` (frontmatter), `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` (loaded as instructions), `BUILD-LOG.md` (deterministic generator with a `--check`; a date would make it fail daily), `.github/` templates, `scores/` and `reports/` (written by the scripts that own them), fixtures. Issue templates carry the same levels as fields: Area (label), Feature (`Scenario:`), Criterion (`F###.n` in the title), and Journey when the PM's check changes.

**Gardening.** The `tend-docs` skill (`scripts/tend_docs.py`) inventories every Markdown doc in `socialus-web`, `socialus-plan`, `socialus-ops` and `skills` each week, before the Friday launch report, and on demand. It finds exact and overlapping duplicates, unreferenced and superseded docs, undated docs, docs without the standard header, hand-written docs that a script could generate, and broken links. On its own it adds headers, unlinks dead links, and deletes empty, exactly duplicated or explicitly superseded docs (repointing links to the kept one), one PR per repo, merged on green. It never changes a doc under `product/`, `DECISIONS.md`, `constraints/`, the charter, mission, voice or legal text; those, and any merge where the canonical doc is not obvious, go to the PM as at most three A/B items a week. Its counts (docs, duplicates, undated, non-conforming, hand-written share) land in `scores/tend-docs/latest.json`, feed `score-doc-drift`, and appear in the Meta-layer trial block (Issue #89), so the trend is visible and the tuning review can propose changes. The per-repo generator `regen-doc-inventory` (`npm run docs:inventory` in `socialus-web`) is the detailed view of one repo and checks the same header.

**Sessions and restarts.** A Dispatch session's memory is a cache and has been wiped before (`process/DISPATCH.md`), so the state needed to resume is saved as a file, not remembered. On "save state", "end of day" and every 5am/5pm handoff, the `dispatch-handoff` skill writes **`handoff/state/YYYY-MM-DD.md`** in `socialus-plan` (one file per day, overwritten by a later save that day, the 14 newest kept, git holding the rest) beside the status snapshot `handoff/latest.md`. It carries the standard header and four sections: **running sessions** (title, repo and worktree, branch, what it is doing, what it is waiting on); **Don's open calls, in order** (the single next item first, each as A/B/C with a recommendation and the PR, Issue or doc that holds it); **decided but not built** (each ruling with no Issue, PR or scenario carrying it yet, with its `DECISIONS.md` date and where it should land); and **the next action**, one line. To resume, a fresh Dispatch on "catch me up" reads the newest state file, verifies every line against GitHub (`gh pr view`, `gh issue view`, `gh run list`) and the session list before repeating it, reports what changed since the save in one line each, drops what no longer holds from the next save, and only then runs the handoff. Nothing in a snapshot is acted on until it is verified; the file tells the next session where to look, GitHub says what is true. Task sessions keep their own state the same way they always have: a handoff note in the PR body at the shift change.

**Renames.** No mechanical rename is needed: the IDs already sit in file names (`F###-slug.md`, `scenario-F###.md`) or in JSON (`J##`). Proposed, not done, because they touch rulings and need the PM: move the undated design notes `planning/{AGENT-ANSWERING,ITEMS-QUESTION,ONE-MODEL,PAGE-KINDS,STALENESS,URL-IDENTITY,VOCABULARY-PROPOSAL}.md` to `planning/notes/<slug>.md` with the standard header; they define page kinds, URL identity and vocabulary.

## 4. Criterion roll-up

**One name for the whole thing.** The *criterion roll-up* is the chain that scores every acceptance criterion, rolls the scores up (criterion, feature, area, milestone), and puts them on the dashboard. Its per-feature artifact is the *criterion report*. The same words are used in the dashboard header and section titles, the audit, the skills and this file [V].

```
 scenario criteria (plan) --+                      +-- phone checklist #519 (ticks) --+
 guards markers / evals ----+--> criterion report -+-- uat Issues -------------------+--> PM looked
 PR review, smoke ----------+    (regen-criterion-report)                              |
                                     |                                                |
                          socialus-plan/scripts/criteria.py   <------------------------+
                          (parses the reports; Checked from markers.py; Smoked, PM looked from runs and labels)
                                     |-> handoff/capabilities.md
                                     v
                          rollup(): criterion -> feature -> area -> milestone  (plain sums)
                                     v
                          dashboard.py (workflow: every push to main, and every 6 h) -> DASHBOARD.md + status-dashboard.html
```

**Where each step lives**

| Step | What does it | Trigger | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| Criteria | Cowork writes the scenario `Acceptance` list, the PM approves | a scenario is approved | 47 scenario files; 26 approved or building [V] |
| Criterion report | `regen-criterion-report` writes `socialus-web/build-log/reports/<area>/F###-<slug>.md`; every gap becomes an Issue | the all-feature run on 2026-10-10; the Friday refresh | 29 of 29 reportable features have one [V] |
| Parse and score | `socialus-plan/scripts/criteria.py` | each dashboard run | 235 criteria [V] |
| Phone checklist | `regen-uat-checklist` keeps issue #519 (label `uat`): 99 boxes, 9 sittings, launch-gated features first; a ticked box is "PM looked" for that criterion | the Friday task | 0 of 99 ticked [V] |
| Capabilities | `criteria.py --capabilities` -> `handoff/capabilities.md` | Friday task | generated 2026-10-10 [V] |
| Dashboard | `dashboard.py`, run by `.github/workflows/dashboard.yml` | push to main, every 6 h, dispatch | last scheduled run did not fire (section 8) [V] |
| Audit | `regen-criterion-audit` -> `audits/criterion-rollup.md` | on request, Friday | regenerated this snapshot [V] |

**Formulas** (all plain sums, none an average of features or a count of Issues):
- A criterion is **built** only when its report row says `yes`; `unknown` counts as unmet.
- **Checked** = a guards marker covers the whole criterion (`markers.py coverage`, the same count as STATUS). **Reviewed** = the row says yes. **Smoked** = a green smoke-live run came after the feature's last merge (pages load; not behaviour). **PM looked** = a ticked box in a `uat` Issue, or `pm-reviewed` on a linked Issue.
- Feature = criteria met / total. Area and milestone = the sum of their criteria. The beta % is **criteria met / total**; Issues closed is shown beside it, not as the headline.
- A feature or area is **red** when an unmet criterion links an open `launch-blocking` Issue. A report older than its last merged PR is flagged **stale**.

**Today** [V, dashboard regenerated 2026-10-11]: 141 of 235 criteria met (60%) across 29 features; checked 40, reviewed 16, smoked 114, PM looked 1; 9 features red (F058, F076, F078, F081, F082, F093, F100, F101, F102); Issues closed 69 of 124.

**The PM's part.** Open https://github.com/donlafranchi/socialus-web/issues/519 on a phone and tick what you looked at; closing a `uat` Issue with every box ticked labels what it names `pm-reviewed` (`uat-close.yml`). Reporting, removing, hiding or publishing steps say to use a test Page. `record-pm-review` takes "<thing> ok" or "<thing> broken: why".

**Second track, not reconciled [V].** `scripts/criteria.py` in this repo (merged, #94) treats a JSON sidecar next to each report as the truth and renders the tables from it. The dashboard does not use it. Its companions, `socialus-web` #659 and `skills` #17, are open. The live roll-up parses the markdown reports. Until one is chosen, edits to a report's format belong in neither track alone.

## 7. Meta layer (**TRIAL**, started 2026-10-10)

The PM's instruction: *stick with this and keep improving it.* The trial is **tuning, not a go/no-go**; dropping it is not an option. Tuning review 2026-10-24: is each score measuring what it should (false reds and misses, with examples), what to adjust, which score is next. Tracker: [#89](https://github.com/donlafranchi/socialus-ops/issues/89), pinned.

**Built:** the `pm-approved` guard (`scripts/pm-approved-guard.cjs`, now also protecting `scripts/score_*.py` and `scripts/trial_health.py`), `score-ci-health`, `score-doc-drift`, `score-gap-leakage`, `scripts/trial_health.py`. **Not built:** `score-review-coverage`, `score-rework`, `score-pm-overrule`, and the reviewer `review-pipeline`.

| Score | Signal | Reading (2026-10-11) |
|---|---|---|
| `score-ci-health` | CI fail %, red scheduled workflows, smoke red %, repos whose Actions cannot start | CI fail 26.3% (red); smoke red 100% of 2 scheduled runs (red); Actions blocked in `skills` (red) [V] |
| `score-doc-drift` | generated-doc age, skill list vs `link.sh` vs table, README claims, approved scenarios with every Issue closed | last reading 2026-10-10: 11 items (red) [V `scores/`] |
| `score-gap-leakage` | closed Issues hiding unmet criteria; unmet criteria with no open Issue; built criteria with no marked check | 16 features, 21 criteria, 74.5% (all red; first reading, with tuning notes on what is likely a false red) [V `scores/`] |

**Governance** (trimmed 2026-10-11, PM-approved). A PR that touches a score skill, a score script, `trial_health.py` or the guard is one of two kinds. `meta-change`: what a score measures or its target changes; the PR body says in plain words what it measured before and after, and only the PM's `pm-approved` label after the last commit merges it. `meta-bookkeeping`: renames, lists, counts, wording; merges on green and the PM never sees it. A protected-file PR with neither label fails until the agent picks one. The guard is a tripwire, not a lock: agents act with the owner's token, so `trial_health.py` counts bookkeeping merges for the Friday review, and in `skills` (private, Actions blocked) the guard runs by hand (`scripts/pm-approved-check.cjs`). Precedents: Kubernetes requires a `kind/*` label on every PR and lets cleanup kinds skip release review (https://prow.k8s.io/command-help, `require-matching-label`); Rust's `rollup=always` marks trivial PRs that merge in batches without their own review (https://forge.rust-lang.org/release/rollups.html); Dependabot's `automerge` label (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot). [V]

**Still to build from the same ruling:** a Pipeline health panel at the top of the daily dashboard showing only the two numbers the PM owns, docs current (stale or undated docs under 5) and overrule rate (how often the PM reverses an agent's plan or recommendation; lower is better); and three silent alarms, main green (95%+), reviews happen (90%+), nothing closes half-built (0), surfaced to the PM only if one stays red. Tracked in [#106](https://github.com/donlafranchi/socialus-ops/issues/106). [P]

**Reminder.** Every Friday the launch report and the dashboard carry a "Meta-layer trial" block (`trial_health.py --block`) and the run writes `scores/tuning/YYYY-MM-DD.md`.

## 11. Changing the method

Branch `process-YYYY-MM-DD-slug`, commit `docs: what`, name the dated failure as the changed rule's "because", open a PR, merge when `lint` is green. This repo is public: nothing secret, legal or personal goes in it.
